So none of them does any of those wicked effects that preceded for the deniers, and they attained perfection through the soundness of the practical faculty, which arises from the soundness of the cognitive faculty. He increased the encouragement by an allusion to the garden of the heart and the expansion of the spirit [ وبَسْطِ الرُّوحِ ] by his saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, meaning the one who does good to them, in the place of those people's regret and the frustration of their hopes, for their being brought near indicates His pleasure, glory be to Him, and the pleasure of the owner of the abode is sought before looking at the abode. When he alluded to the garden of the heart, he followed it with the garden of the heart [ جَنَّةَ القَلْبِ ] and said, may He be exalted: ﴿gardens﴾, plural of jannah, which linguistically is a comprehensive orchard, and in the usage of the Sharia it is a place in which all joy has gathered and from which all evil has been removed, ﴿of bliss (al-na'im)﴾, which is that which is pure of turbidity, disturbance and vexation, with nothing in it other than that at all, by what the construction of the genitive (al-idafah) conveys.

Since the non-inheritance by either of the two groups of the abode whose description has preceded would amount to equating the good-doer with the evil-doer, and since that is not befitting for a Wise One to do, its denial became necessary, to confirm that what Allah, glorified is He, has reported can only be as such. This is especially so since the disbelievers used to say that they were like the Muslims or in a better condition than them. That is because, if there is no resurrection, as they used to suppose, then they are equal after death, along with what they were preferred for in this world through following their desires and obtaining pleasures. And if there is a resurrection, then they used to say, out of a doubt that their desire had led them to: "Will we not, on the assumption of it, be in a better condition than you and more favoured with Allah in pleasant living, just as we are in this abode? For He has extended nothing to us in this abode except that we are better than you in His sight." So the Exalted said, denying that and rejecting it in the strongest terms, and blaming the arbitrary judgment made in ignorance in the most extreme way, negating equality, so that it would be a retribution that is higher than the sphere of "how much more so," causing it by what its supposed meaning is: "And that would not be for other than the God-fearing": ﴿Shall We then treat the Muslims﴾, that is, those who are firmly rooted in submission to Our commands and in joining what We commanded to be joined, seeking Our good pleasure, so they have no choice with Us in any soul or otherwise, due to the goodness of their natures, ﴿like the criminals﴾, that is, those who are firmly rooted in severing what We commanded [to be joined], and you do not accept the like of that. Rather, whoever opposes you in any kind of opposition, you sever ties with him, even if the matter reaches killing.

(p-319) When this proof had removed the doubts and lifted the veil, bringing it to something brighter than the light of day, he turned the speech toward them with direct address, like one who is angry while rebuking. So He said, marveling at them and alerting them to the crookedness of their natural disposition and the corruption of their thinking, denouncing them in the strongest terms: ﴿What is wrong with you?﴾ That is, what is it that befalls you from these unjust rulings, far from the truth?

When He had alerted them that they have no benefit whatsoever in such rulings, and it is the way of the intelligent person that when he knows something has no benefit in it, he distances himself from it, He denounced them a third time over the state of these rulings of theirs, because negating their states is stronger in negating them, as was mentioned in ﴿How can you disbelieve?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28] in al-Baqarah. So He said: ﴿How do you judge?﴾ That is, what intellect has prompted you to this judgment, which entails equating, on the part of the master, between the good among his servants and the evildoer?

Since a judgment cannot exist except when it is qualified by some manner, and since Glorified and Exalted is He has negated their judgment by denying all the manners by which it could be valid, and since a sound judgment must be grounded either in reason ('aql) or in transmission (naql), the falsehood of their judgment became further evident by negating both together. So He said, linking it (conjunctively) to what is implied by its context: "Do you have a proof from reason to which you resort?" ﴿Or do you have a Book﴾, that is, a known heavenly scripture, recognized as being from Allah, specific to you, ﴿in which﴾, that is, not in any other, from the fables of the ancients and the scriptures of the annihilated ones, ﴿you study﴾, that is, you read with a reading in which you have become thoroughly acquainted with it, or in which you have made its understanding excellent through it.

Having mentioned the lesson (al-dars), He then mentioned what is studied (al-madrus), saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, for you﴾, that is, specifically, in the manner of emphasis which admits no leniency in abandoning it, ﴿in it﴾, that is, in the Book, so that you may be in the utmost confidence in it, and not in other than it, of which you have no confidence, ﴿is that which you choose﴾, that is, you exert yourselves in selecting it and taking its best parts. The hamza in inna is kasra-ed, though its proper vowel would be fatha were it not for the lam (la), because what follows it is the thing studied. It is also permissible for the sentence to be a quotation of what is studied, and also permissible for it to be a resumptive (isti'nafiyya) sentence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 68, verse 39:

When he had negated the proof of reason and transmitted revelation, together with expressing wonder at them and mocking them, and it remained that a person may sometimes pledge to another something and then be bound to fulfil it even if it is outside what reason and transmitted revelation call for, he negated that with His saying: ﴿Or do you have oaths upon Us⦗⦘ that are binding⦗⦘ to the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is: oaths that are extremely firm, ﴿upon Us﴾, which you have imposed upon Us, ﴿binding﴾, that is (p-321) by reason of their greatness they reach the utmost degrees of emphasis, such that the attainment of any other oath, compared to their attainment, is as nothing; that is, their attainment is the attainment itself and nothing else. Or their permanence ends ﴿at the Day of Resurrection﴾, so that release from their obligation is not possible except on that Day, so that you would need them for your honour in both abodes.

When he had mentioned that oath by oaths, he mentioned the thing sworn to, saying: ﴿Indeed, for you⦗⦘ is whatever you decide⦗⦘.﴾ That is, specifically for you, to the exclusion of the Muslims, ﴿whatever you decide﴾, that is, what you do in the manner of a judge whose word is binding because of the elevation of his authority, in a way of emphasis from which there is no escape, so that you decide for yourselves whatever good you desire.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 68, verse 40:

When He marveled at them and mocked them, He followed that with a mockery greater than theirs, which exposes their deficiency to the utmost exposure and brings upon them the most severe destruction. So He said, warning them against turning away: ﴿Ask them﴾, i.e., O Messenger, whose proofs have eclipsed all lights by the strength of their radiance.

Since asking is a cause for the attainment of knowledge, "sal" (ask) was made to take its second object, and its proper construction was with "ʿan" (about). So He said: ﴿Which of them will stand surety for that?﴾, i.e., the great matter of the covenant and the transmitted and rational proof. ﴿Surety﴾ means guarantor and bail-giver, or leader, or chief, or one who speaks with truth or falsehood, so that he is bound in his claim to the soundness of that, (p-322) which would make him a laughing-stock for the servants and a marvel to those present among them and the desert-dwellers. None of them dared, given what you know of the truth of this Qur'an and the ancientness in falsehood of all their sayings, despite the intensity of their enmity, their love of contention, and their arrogance, to come forward to claim that.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 68, verse 41:

When He negated that they could have from Him, glorified is He, any rational proof, or transmitted proof, or firm covenant regarding their equating themselves with the Muslims in this [sound and firm] arrangement and most upright path, He followed it with what might come from others, if there were any such, [showing] that they were in error in what they claimed. So He said: ﴿Or have they partners?﴾ That is, they have legislated for them some matter of religion and promised them something, and they have set up for it such proofs as We have set up for Our Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Then let them bring their partners﴾ That is, with their statements and their deeds, just as We have brought, in support of Our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, both of these matters together, with what is beyond any doubt. He also recorded against them, in the Book, [words that are] inflaming and stirring, with that which burns their livers and which they cannot repel in any way. That will be the greatest proof of their falsehood. So He said: ﴿If they are truthful﴾ That is, by nature and disposition, ﴿truthful﴾, that is, steeped in this attribute as they claim. When He had negated all the doubts with which they could cling, along with the clarification of His capacity to do what He wills, through the unfolding of proofs and the splitting open of demonstrations, which indicates the perfection of knowledge and, from it, the perfection of power, He brought them, from the clarity of the matter, to a point where nothing remained except obstinacy. He followed that with a threat to them with what establishes His power over it, from the Day of Judgment, and His dealing with them justly on it. So He said:

[yawm] may be an explanatory apposition (bayān) to Yawm al-Qiyāma (the Day of Resurrection), and it is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is attached to a clause. It may also be an adverb of time (ẓarf) governing ya'tū (they will come), or it may be in the accusative (manṣūb) by what is implied from the meaning of the statement, [such as]: "They will know what they will suffer as the consequence of these dealings, even if they attained all the pleasures of this world throughout the whole of the day in which ﴿the shin is uncovered﴾," meaning the day in which the uncovering takes place. It was made passive (mabnī lil-maf'ūl) because what is frightening is the occurrence of the uncovering, which is a metaphor (kināya) for the aggravation of affairs and their exceeding the limit of endurance, not for it being caused by a specific agent, although it is well known that there is no agent there other than Him, glorified is He. ﴿ʿan sāq﴾ ("of a shin") means that the matter will become extremely severe in it, because whoever is overwhelmed by a matter and strives to resolve it rolls up his shin (shammara ʿan sāqihi) for its sake, and women's [garments] are rolled up from their shins, uncovering themselves without modesty, out of flight. Thus it is a metaphor for this, and for this reason it is indefinite (nakkarahu), to express its awfulness [for it] and magnification. This interpretation is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, and from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, and others. It is also [interpreted as] the uncovering of all realities and the manifestation in it of great and subtle matters, of terrors and other things, just as these verses uncovered all doubts and left the listener with them as in the light of day. In the thirty-fifth section of the Musnad of Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī, on the authority of Abū Burda, on the authority of his father, may Allah be pleased with him, [who said that] the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning this:

"From a great light, they will fall down prostrating to it." This does not contradict the two interpretations mentioned: the severity and the uncovering. Since this uncovering that revealed to them the meanings in this Qur'an is only for the sake of worship, which is submission expressed by prostration, and it is its sign (āya) and the indication of what the inner self contained of it and its mark, they will come to it while they are able to do it. He reminded them of a day on which they would wish to do it, but it will not be possible for them, as a reproach to them, an increase of their regret, and a display of humiliation and loss. For their backs and their limbs will be one solid piece that does not bend, so whenever they wish to prostrate, they will turn over onto their backs. He said [it] with the passive form, indicating their desire for submission and their eagerness for it from whatever motive it came, and it indicates that obligation does not end except when each of the two groups enters its abode. ﴿And they will be called﴾, meaning by the summons of the Sovereign, the Judge, ﴿to prostration﴾, as a rebuke for abandoning it now, and as reproach and censure, not as worship or obligation. So they will wish for it in order to avoid harm to themselves from what they see of terrors. ﴿But they cannot﴾, meaning it results from that that they ﴿are not able﴾, because they are not sound: they have no limbs that obey them for it, despite their intense striving with themselves. Moreover, their limbs will not be docile to what this form of speech conveys, namely that if one of them wishes to do an act and strives for it with force but is unable to do it, their backs will be in a state in which they do not bend; rather, the vertebrae (al-safāfīd) will be in them. So they will feel the greatest regret for having abandoned it in the world while they were able to do it, and it was then beneficial to them [while their striving to perform it most intensely and their inability to do it, it being no longer beneficial to them]. When they fail despite their striving, they will be even more incapable without it. That is because a person is raised on what he died upon and gathered on what he was raised upon: if good, then good; if evil, then evil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 68, verse 43:

Since someone might suppose that what prevents them is arrogance, as in this world, He said, clarifying the negation of arrogance on such a great day: ﴿Their eyes will be humbled﴾, that is, submissive and lowly, "because what is in the heart is recognized in the eye. The believers raise their heads and faces brighter than the sun, while the faces of the disbelievers and the hypocrites are black and dark."

Since the one who is humbled in this way may be humbled out of some good that he has, while holding on to might, He said: ﴿Humiliation will cover them﴾, that is, envelop them and overpower them, ﴿great humiliation﴾, because they used the limbs that He, glory be to Him and exalted, had given them, so that they might draw near to Him in the abode of action, in enjoying what distances them from Him.

Since this expression, in agreement with what is related in the sound hadith, indicates that whoever had a disease in his heart in this world will have his back become one single plate, one single vertebra, so that when he tries to prostrate he will turn over onto his back, He marvelled at them for persisting in injustice, which is placing a thing in other than its proper place, and said: ﴿And they had been﴾, that is, while the state was that they ﴿had been﴾ constantly, through the established address, ﴿being called﴾ in the world by every caller who calls to Us ﴿to prostration, and they﴾, that is, refusing it, while the state was that they ﴿were sound﴾, that is, [they were] able, with nothing in their limbs preventing them from that, and it was only pride and arrogance that prevented them from it. Thus the verse is of the type of *al-ihtibak* (mutual omission): mentioning the inability first indicates the omission of ability second, and mentioning soundness second indicates the omission of unsoundness first.

(p-326) When he knew from this that He, glorified is He, alone disposes of what He wills, as He wills, in withholding and in granting power, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was suffering from their denial of him, despite his bringing what cannot admit of denial in any way, a hardship whose measure none knows except Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and since the one who is distressed knows that he has a rescuer who will ease his burden, and since his knowledge of His power over what is sought from Him was more comforting to his eye, the cause of His complete power is His saying, easing his burden, upon him be the best of blessings and peace, turning the speech to the first person singular for explicit specification of the intended meaning, as an increase in calming the heart and expanding the breast: ﴿Leave Me alone﴾, i.e., leave Me in whatever state it happens to be, ﴿and whoever denies this discourse﴾, i.e., whoever brings denial upon the one who recites what I have renewed the sending down of from My eternal speech, in whatever state that denial occurs. He made the pronoun singular explicitly to threaten each one of the deniers: ﴿this discourse﴾, i.e., because of it. That is, leave Me to deal with them, entrust their affair to Me, and do not concern yourself with any of it at all, for I will suffice you against them, since there is no preventer from them, so do not be concerned with them at all.

And since it was as if it were said: "And what will you do with it if you leave between you and it?" (p-327) He answered him with His saying, gathering the pronoun so that the one [among them] is threatened a fortiori: ﴿We will draw them on step by step﴾, i.e., We will seize them by Our majesty before long, unawares, by a promise that admits no breach, and bring them near to destruction degree by degree, through whomever We will of Our hosts, and without intermediary, by continually bestowing upon them blessings that obligate them to gratitude, so they make these a cause for increased disbelief, and so We make punishments obligatory for them. And since seizing a person from his place of safety while he is heedless, by entangling him in the causes of destruction, so that he perceives the destruction only when he is unable to escape from it in any way, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿from where﴾, i.e., from directions, ﴿they do not know﴾, i.e., there does not renew for them knowledge of its perils at any moment of time. That is because He, glorified is He, deceives them with respite and does not hasten their punishment at the time of their disobedience, as happens to one for whom good is intended and so he awakens; rather He gives them respite and provides them with blessings until the thought of remembrance departs from them, so they are blessed outwardly and drawn toward ruin in reality. They say: "You have said that decree (qadar) overflows from judgement (qaḍāʾ), and that deeds are judgement while their recompense is decree." They also say: "Our deeds in this world are ugly, and we see no recompense for them except what pleases us. Were it not so, Allah would punish us for what we say, so you are liars in your threat to us, for whenever we originate what you call disobedience, a blessing renews for us." That is like how it led them to be drawn on (p-328) while they were in the utmost desire. Al-Qushayri said: Istidraj (gradual drawing toward ruin) is that He wills evil for a person and conceals from him the face of intent until He seizes him suddenly, drawing him on to it thing after thing.

Because istidraj (gradual lead-on toward ruin) occurs through many means, including the extension of blessings and other things, He expressed it with the nun shared between the plural of self-association and the plural of majesty. And since the postponement of the term can only belong to God alone, without any intermediary, He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And I give them respite﴾, meaning: I alone postpone their terms and extend for them all their enjoyment, so that they increase in sin, ﴿for them﴾, because none other than Me can extend the term and grant ease of life.

When He had consoled him, peace be upon him, with this to the utmost degree of consolation, He gave the reason for it, or began a new statement in answer to one who might say: "Were they not of this condition?", naming His favor a stratagem: ﴿Indeed My plan is firm﴾, meaning: My concealing from the one I want to destroy the causes of ruin, and My displaying that to him in garments of kindness and the mantle of goodness and bounty. ﴿Firm﴾, meaning: in the utmost strength, since it causes the human being to bring about his own destruction by his own choice. "And he will know when the seizing comes that when I granted him respite, I did not neglect him, and that (p-329) My granting respite was only istidraj."

When this Qur'an was the greatest of blessings, He, glory be to Him and exalted, brought it to them. It therefore necessitated that they give thanks for the One who sent it down and for honoring the one who brought it. Yet it became a cause for them to engage in denial [of it] [ بِهِ -] and harm toward the one who brought it to them, which necessitated their seizure. He said, indicating the firmness of His plan, glory be to Him, and the subtlety of His gradual leading-on [ عَلى -]. Conjoining it to what is implied, to show that they engage in what destroys them by their own choice without any compelling cause: "Is their denial of this Reminder because of something about which they have doubt?" Its statement rebukes them and clarifies that their denial is only because it is a disposition, baseness and innate nature, with no desire or doubt in it: ﴿Or do you ask them﴾, you, O most chaste of creation and highest in aspirations, ﴿for a wage﴾ for your conveying it to them, ﴿so that they are﴾, that is, so that as a consequence of that and as a result, they ﴿burdened by debt﴾ from the obligation they have been made to bear, so that they are ﴿weighed down﴾, that is, actually weighed down by it, to the extent that this debt diminishing their wealth made them hold back from affirming what you brought to them from Us, so they came to wish that you would cease from it.

When he had negated that their denial stemmed from a desire that prompted them to it, he negated that they had any doubt about the Reminder [or any injustice in what was mentioned], or that they were confident or had a presumption of a good outcome. So he said: ﴿Or do they have the unseen﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿so that they write it down﴾, meaning, whatever they wish to write from it, having obtained knowledge from the Preserved Tablet or elsewhere, ﴿therefore they write﴾, by reason of that. That is, so that they may have become aware that this Reminder is not from Allah, or aware that there is no reckoning upon them for denying it. Thus it is known from this that they have no ordinary desire for that, nor any doubt. Rather, their denial is merely the wickedness of natures, the darkness of souls, and empty wishes and covetous hopes.

When all of that was negated, it became established that they were in a great peril. He, glory be to Him, is the One uniquely knowing the unseen, and He had informed of their destruction on account of him (ﷺ). The disbelief of whoever disbelieved and the faith of whoever believed are by His decree and destiny, so both had to occur. This was a cause that moved him (ﷺ) to patience until the time that He, glory be to Him, appointed for relief. So He said, giving the reason for what is implied: none of what was mentioned belonged to him; it is only decree and destiny: ﴿So be patient﴾, that is, with the utmost patience and the most complete patience, over what they say about you and over other things, and over all the bitter decree and destiny that comes from them and from others. ﴿For the judgment of your Lord﴾, that is, for the decree that He decreed and determined, the One who is good to you, who honored you with what He honored you with of the message, and charged you with what He charged you with of conveying it, and abandoned them to denial, and extended their lives for that, and widened blessings upon them, and delayed what He promised you of victory. ﴿And do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, that is, your condition should not be in impatience and haste or otherwise.

Since the surah began with the letter nun, whose connotation includes the fish (al-hut), he expressed it here to confirm its intention, and so He said: ﴿like the companion of the fish﴾, that is, like the condition of the companion of the fish, who is Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, ﴿when﴾, that is, the time when. The governing element of this adverbial phrase, whose noun is omitted, is a state or the like; or the implied meaning is: your condition should not be like his, so that there befalls you what befell him when ﴿he called out﴾, that is, to his Lord, the Nurturer who cared for him with His goodness, in the darknesses of the belly of the fish, and the darkness of what surrounds him of the mass, and the darkness of the depths of the seas. ﴿And he was﴾, that is, and the state was that at the time of his calling, ﴿distressed﴾, that is, filled with anguish, grief, severity, and sorrow, carried by silence in his belly, so he did not speak because of the intensity of his sadness, and restrained from all that he wished to do, until He, glory be to Him, drove him by that to supplication and humble entreaty. It is from kazm, which is silence over fullness and swallowing of bitternesses; from this is "kazamtu al-siqa'" meaning I tightened it and filled it, so it became "maktum." The "makdum" is the one in distress, as if he had been seized by his throat while he was expelling his soul.

When the listener was eager to know what became of him after this wondrous matter, [God] said: ﴿Had it not been that﴾, and the favour was magnified by the reminder and by the form of the verb (tafā'ul, the reciprocal verbal form), so He said: ﴿a grace from his Lord overtook him﴾, i.e., overtook him with a great overtaking, which was a blessing and a favour at once, wishing that it overtake [the other -] ﴿a blessing﴾, i.e., very great, ﴿from his Lord﴾, i.e., the One who sent him and showed him kindness by sending him and refining him for the message, and by accepting his repentance and showing him mercy. ﴿He would certainly have been cast﴾, i.e., were it not for this lofty state with which God favoured him, he would have been thrown down with a very easy throwing ﴿into the open desert﴾, i.e., the barren land with no building or plant in it, far from people, where he was cast as God had decreed from eternity, ﴿while he was﴾, i.e., while the state was that he was ﴿blameworthy﴾, i.e., blamed for the sin.

Since the sense is: "But his Lord reached him with grace, so he was not blameworthy in being cast out," he (God) connected to this His words: ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, that is, He selected him for His message, ﴿his Lord﴾. Then, as a consequence of his being chosen, He connected His words: ﴿and made him among the righteous﴾, that is, among those who were firmly established in the rank of righteousness, so that they became upright in themselves for prophethood and messengership, and others were made upright through them. Thus he was cast out onto the open plain while he was praiseworthy, and whoever is patient greater than his patience has a greater reward than his reward. You are likewise, so you are the most noble of those who act and of the worlds.

When the Prophet ﷺ was forbidden to obey the deniers, warned against being lax toward them (*idhān*), and struck examples for them, and when He threatened them, He said, ﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse. We will draw them on gradually﴾ (al-Qalam 68:44). He concluded with the story of Yūnus, peace be upon him, to train him in patience and to avoid weakness, even slightly leaning toward the one who is lax (*al-mudhin*). The implied meaning, as a cause of what was forbidden in it, is: "They only exaggerate in harming you so that you become impatient and abandon what you are upon." He then said, joining this implied meaning with a conjunction, informing him of the resentment in their breasts toward him and the rancor in their hearts against him, so that his caution against their laxity would intensify. It is emphasized because whoever sees their laxity assumes their submission, and their excessive display of it hides their transgression. (p-334) ﴿And indeed﴾, that is, and indeed ﴿they nearly﴾. The noun was made explicit instead of the pronoun to generalize and to tie the judgment to the attribute, so He said, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who concealed what they were able to conceal of the proofs you brought.

Since "*nūn*" was lightened, He brought the *lām* that marks it, so He said, ﴿they would surely make you slip﴾, that is, out of the intensity of their enmity, envy, and the seething of their hearts, ﴿with their eyes﴾, that is, they would bring about your removal from what you are in, and the great slip that accompanies it, in a place of slipperiness with no firm footing, leading to destruction and what is less than it of harm, until they throw you down from your stature to the ground, as a person slips and is thrown down, due to what appears in their eyes when they fix their gaze with fury and wrath, which indicates that their breasts are boiling. This is from their saying, "He looked at me with a look that nearly felled me," meaning, if he were able to fell me with it, he would have felled me, as Allah the Exalted said, ﴿they nearly assault those who recite Our verses to them﴾ (al-Hajj 22:72). It has also been said: they would destroy you by striking with the evil eye. Al-Qushayri said: when they wanted to strike something with their eyes, they would go hungry for three days, then look at that thing and say, "How beautiful is this thing!" and the object looked at would fall immediately. They did this to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "How sincere a man he is!" but Allah protected him from them. Al-Shaykhayn narrated from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, (p-335) that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"The evil eye is real." In a narration in Aḥmad and Ibn Mājah: "The devil is present with it, and the envy of the son of Ādam." Aḥmad also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, in a marfūʿ report: "The evil eye is real, and if anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it. And when you are asked to wash (for the cure), then wash." Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilyah narrated from the hadith of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, in a marfūʿ report: "The evil eye is real; it brings the camel into the pot and the man into the grave." Abū Dāwūd narrated from the hadith of Asmāʾ bint Yazīd, may Allah be pleased with her: "Indeed it overtakes the rider and makes him stumble."

When He mentioned this great slipping, He mentioned its time, expressing it in the past tense to remind of the past state, so He said, ﴿when they heard the Reminder﴾, that is, the Qur'an, in which reminding predominates over matters that every person raises up from himself and from the horizons. Their desire was first to hear it out of envy for what you were given of honor. Their hearing it became the motive for the hatred and envy they harbored, so that the passage of time only increased their rage, as indicated by ﴿and they say﴾, that is, a statement they never cease to renew.

Since he ﷺ was at the furthest extreme from what would blemish him, they emphasized their statement: ﴿Indeed, he is mad!﴾, out of bewilderment regarding your matter and to repel people from you, because they know that no one hears it without having no purpose except their lies, and that he inclines wholly toward you, stays with you, becomes attached to you, and rejoices in what you have brought. (p-336) It is reported from al-Ḥasan that reciting this verse is a cure for being struck by the evil eye.

Since the meaning of their saying was that what he says is the jumbled talk of one afflicted by jinn, He emphasized, with restrictive emphasis (qasr al-qalb), His statement, expressing wonder at them: ﴿And it is not﴾ — that is, while the case is that this Qur'an, or the Messenger ﷺ, is not ﴿anything but a reminder﴾ — that is, an admonition and an honor ﴿for the worlds﴾ — that is, all of them, high and low among them. There is none of them who does not know that nothing resembles it in the majesty of its meanings, the sweetness of its words, the greatness of its composition, the precision of its understanding, the delicacy of its margins, and the sturdiness of its arrangement. Each one understands from it according to what Allah has prepared him for, so that the universality of its being a reminder matches the universality of the message for the one to whom it is sent. Everything in it of promise and threat, rulings and admonitions, is comprehensive for all of them. Therefore the distinction between their believers and their criminals became necessary, so that its statements may be true and its majesty and beauty be perfected. Its conclusion has returned, as you see, to its opening with the "Nun" and the pen and "what they write" concerning this reminder, and it negated what they said about it, of madness and of swearing by the great creation, which is this wise reminder. It alerted, by its being a reminder for all creation with what it contains of promise and threat, that there must be the Inevitable Reality (al-Haqqah), which is the Resurrection, so that its interpretation, its summary and its detail may become manifest therein, and its path may become clear in the utmost clarity, (p-337) and its realities may be established therein and its great and fine points may appear through what occurs of reckoning, and it may be made utterly clear, and error may become evident from truth. And Allah is the Guide.
